name: The Passenger Protocol (BCI Grief Flash)
description: The Passenger Protocol is a coordinated BCI flash event that activates spontaneously among users within a half-kilometer radius whenever a registered participant dies — the network broadcasts a 30-second loop of that person's most-shared sensory memory directly into the neural feeds of everyone nearby, creating a sudden shared experience of the deceased's perspective. Originally designed in 2208 by grief counselor and BCI developer Miriam Achterberg-Sato as an opt-in memorial network for the Shelf, the Protocol has grown to over 400,000 registered participants across all tiers and occasionally triggers in unexpected locations, flooding Tier 4 boardrooms or transit hubs with the last joyful memory of a Shelf child or the final working moment of a synthetic being. The phenomenon is structurally legal but socially disruptive enough that three corponations have attempted to have it reclassified as a cyberattack.
cultural_impact: The Passenger Protocol has forced a visceral cross-tier confrontation with mortality and inequality — Tier 4 and 5 residents who have never visited the Shelf routinely find themselves experiencing the sensory memories of people whose lives are radically different from their own. It has generated both a significant empathy movement and a significant backlash, with some Tier 4 residents paying for BCI shielding specifically to opt out.
key_figures: Representative Dayo Ferreira-Lundqvist (politician who attempted legal reclassification)
The Protocol Network (decentralized, no central admin)
locations: Originally seeded in the Sump District (Shelf)
Active across all tiers wherever participants are present
The Protocol's founding memorial node is maintained in the Calumet Community Archive
story_hooks: A Tier 5 executive accidentally registered for the Protocol through a legal document they didn't read carefully, and has now experienced three Shelf deaths in two weeks — they want it removed, but the Protocol has no off-switch once registered, and the creator is not cooperating.

Someone is deliberately registering synthetic beings in the Protocol just before their scheduled decommissioning, flooding corporate facilities with synthetic sensory memories as a form of protest — and the campaign is escalating.

A Protocol flash activates in a location where no registered participant should have died, broadcasting a memory that contains clear evidence of a crime — and someone very powerful wants that memory suppressed before it can be traced.
